title: Ops Convocation: SLO Commitment Charter & Escalation Matrix
content:
Objective
-----------
This doc captures the proposal for an "ops convocation" — a focused cross-functional kickoff event and 90-day program to finalize SLO commitments for key model-serving surfaces, define an escalation matrix, and align handoffs between product teams, platform, and SRE. The goal is to produce clear, actionable SLO contracts that teams can sign up to and a lightweight escalation and mitigation pattern for incidents that impact customer-facing latency, throughput, and correctness.

Context / Why now
-------------------
- Recent incidents (see JIRA-1234) exposed unclear ownership when a model-serving rollback was needed under high traffic.
- We are ramping Dedicated customers and need deterministic expectations for latency and error budgets across deployment modes.
- SRE and platform teams need a consistent, minimal escalation ladder to reduce cognitive load during cross-team incident resolution.
- This will feed into the Console rollout and the SLO dashboard ingestion pipeline.

Principles
-----------
1) Keep SLOs measurable and narrow: one SLI per customer-visible promise (latency P99, success-rate, embedding freshness window).
2) Lean escalation: prefer pre-agreed fallbacks (model variant route, regional reroute) to ad-hoc manual fixes.
3) Iterative contracts: first pass is conservative; we tighten as telemetry improves.
4) Cross-functional sign-off: product, platform, and SRE must all sign the SLO doc before it is published.

Scope (what this convocation covers)
------------------------------------
- Service surfaces: hosted API inference (text generation), embeddings API, Dedicated inference pool endpoints.
- SLIs considered: latency (P50/P95/P99), request success rate (200-series), model output correctness proxy (e.g., hallucination triggers from eval set), embedding freshness and completeness.
- Not in scope: billing thresholds, per-customer contractual SLAs (those will be separate legal/finance workstreams).

Key deliverables (90 days)
-------------------------
- SLO Commitment Pack for each surface with owner, SLI definition, measurement source, alert thresholds, and initial error budget.
- Escalation Matrix (4 levels: local owner, platform on-call, cross-team bridge, exec notice) with contact roster and triggers.
- Canary & fallback playbook: steps to failover to lower-cost/ lower-latency model variants or region.
- SLO ingestion checklist for Console dashboards and retention rules (metric names, tags, sampling).
- Post-convocation retrospective and backlog of follow-ups.

Stakeholders & proposed RACI
---------------------------
- Product: Priya Nair (owner for hosted-api SLOs) — Responsible for SLO targets and business impact descriptions.
- Platform (model serving runtime): Marcus Lee — Responsible for measurement instrumentation and circuit-breaker knobs.
- SRE: Asha Patel — Responsible for alerting thresholds, escalation ladder, and runbook scaffolding.
- Solutions / Customer Success: Sofia Martínez — Responsible for customer communication templates and onboarding checklist.
- Observability: Ethan Rivera — Responsible for dashboard templates and query standards.
- Legal/Finance: consult as needed for any SLA->Contract translation.

90-day plan (high level)
------------------------
Weeks 0–2 (Prep and discovery)
- Inventory current SLIs and metrics (Ethan).
- Identify top 6 customer-impacting endpoints from recent telemetry.
- Share pre-read (this doc) and invite reps from product teams.

Week 3 (Convocation event, 4 hrs)
- Half-day working session: agree on candidate SLIs and initial targets for each surface.
- Breakouts: hosted API, embeddings, Dedicated pools.
- Immediate output: one-page SLO sketch per surface and agreed action owners.

Weeks 4–6 (Instrument & validate)
- Platform & Observability implement and validate SLI queries against historical data.
- Run smoke alerts in a sandbox (no paged alerts yet).

Weeks 7–10 (Draft commitments & runbooks)
- Product drafts SLO Commitment Packs.
- SRE assembles escalation matrix and basic runbooks (canary rollback, region reroute, cache flush).

Weeks 11–13 (Sign-off and publishing)
- Cross-functional review and sign-off.
- Publish to Confluence and wire up Console dashboards.
- Communication: announcement to internal teams + customer-facing FAQ draft for CS.

Workstreams (parallel)
---------------------
1) Measurement hygiene (lead: Ethan) — canonical metric names, tags, aggregation windows, sampling.
2) SLO policy templates (lead: Asha) — standard fields, decision criteria for target selection.
3) Escalation & on-call adjustments (lead: Marcus) — define when platform on-call must take bridge, and what automation exists.
4) Customer comms and onboarding (lead: Sofia) — onboarding checklist, FAQ, change notifications.
5) Console integration (lead: Priya) — dashboard templates and retention/alert settings.

Escalation Matrix (proposal)
---------------------------
Trigger categories (examples):
- Severity A: sustained P99 latency > target for 10m AND > error budget burn rate threshold.
- Severity B: intermittent but growing error rate affecting >0.5% of customers for 30m.
- Severity C: single-customer impact or degraded background job affecting internal metrics.

Matrix (simplified)
- Level 1 (Local owner): product engineer(s) — initial investigation, attempt hotfix or rollback.
- Level 2 (Platform on-call): if Level 1 can't remediate in 15–30 mins OR if rollback requires infra toggles.
- Level 3 (Cross-team bridge): if service impact > 30m or multiple regions affected — SRE/Platform/Product + CS join.
- Level 4 (Exec notice): sustained major customer impact or regulatory scope incident — notify VP-level and legal.

Contact roster (stub)
- Hosted API product owner: priya@redwood.ai
- Platform on-call channel: #platform-oncall
- SRE bridge channel: #sre-bridges
- Pager: see internal roster (TBD)

Risk register (top items)
------------------------
- Measurement drift: SLIs defined incorrectly or sampling variance -> mitigation: run 30-day backtest and synthetic traffic suite.
- Overly aggressive targets: teams miss SLOs causing repeated paged incidents -> mitigation: choose conservative first targets and review after 60 days.
- Communication lag: CS not informed of SLO changes -> mitigation: include CS in sign-off and weekly digest.
- Runbook gaps: missing rollback automation -> mitigation: prioritize automation tickets in sprint 1.

Open questions / decisions needed
--------------------------------
- Should Dedicated customer SLOs be expressed as per-customer quotas (absolute) or as percentiles? (Action: product & CS discuss by week 4).
- Acceptable error budget burn policy — automatic throttles or manual gating? (Action: platform ops & SRE).
- Retention policy for SLO telemetry in Console — 90 days or 180 days? (Action: Observability team).

Checklist (for each SLO Commitment Pack)
---------------------------------------
- [ ] SLI defined with exact query and tags
- [ ] Measurement owner assigned
- [ ] Target & error budget defined (SLO percentage, window)
- [ ] Alert thresholds mapped to escalation matrix
- [ ] Fallback canary playbook attached
- [ ] Dashboard and synthetic test added
- [ ] CS communication snippet prepared

Success metrics (how we know this worked)
----------------------------------------
- 80% of targeted SLOs have cross-functional sign-off within 90 days.
- Mean time to identify owner reduced by 30% in incidents affecting model-serving.
- Fewer ad-hoc cross-team escalations (tracked via post-incident surveys).
- Console shows SLO health for surface coverage > 70% of traffic.

Post-convocation retro topics
---------------------------
- Did we pick the right SLIs?
- Were targets realistic?
- How did the escalation matrix perform in tabletop exercises?
- Gaps in automation that blocked remediation.

Immediate next steps (this week)
--------------------------------
- Ethan to produce SLI inventory query and list top 6 endpoints (due 2026-05-18).
- Marcus to draft initial escalation triggers and share with SRE (due 2026-05-20).
- Priya to schedule 4-hr convocation and invite product reps (due 2026-05-19).
- Asha to create SLO Commitment Pack template (due 2026-05-21).

Notes to self (informal)
-----------------------
- Keep the convocation focused: avoid deep architecture debates — surface impact and ownership only.
- Bring a simple synthetic load demo to show noisy neighbor scenario.
- Remember legal might want separate wording before public-facing SLA language.

Appendix: example SLO sketch (hosted generation)
------------------------------------------------
- SLI: request latency P99 for text-generation endpoint for requests with seq_len <= 1024 (tag: service=hosted-gen).
- Measurement: prometheus histogram redwood_service_hosted_gen_request_latency_seconds_bucket{seq_len="<=1024"}.
- SLO: 99.5% over rolling 30d.
- Error budget: 0.5% over 30d.
- Alert: error budget burn rate > 2x in 1h -> Level 2 engage.
- Fallback: route to cached responses for repeated prompts OR route to lighter model variant with known lower latency.

---
End of draft.

Comments welcome — if you want to be at the convocation, please ping in #slo-convocation and add to collaborators here.
